analysis:
The PR only changes docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, adding a new section (head lines 129-153) about an unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate (GLM5NextPagedSparseState, PagedImmutableSnapshot, the native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1 codec). No code, configuration, or deployment changes are included, so no control is weakened by this diff itself.

Relevant threat T-041 (prefix-cache cross-tenant sharing, TTFT oracle, at-rest artifacts) and its detection_hint: any change to the production gate in PrefixCachePolicy needs sign-off. The doc states that SSD eligibility defaults on for EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp via PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel. That is a code-side gating change described in the doc but not visible in this batch. It widens the at-rest and TTFT-oracle surface, but only for an exact model ID that the doc says is outside coordinator-registered serving models. The doc also says it binds the protected tuple's full-state store, that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 opts out, and that complete reuse requires authenticated encrypted restore and charged import/export ownership. These are documented as unchanged controls (the same encrypted DBK3, HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, and cacheSalt scoping), so I see no invalidated assumption.

Open integration questions for later passes: (1) The code adding isGLM5NextDefaultModel and the new codec/store is not supplied, so I cannot confirm that it keeps the HMAC-keyed naming, cacheSalt folding, AAD, and KEK binding. (2) T-041's affected_files and the default-on model list should mention the GLM candidate if the code lands. (3) Partial-page checkpoints and copy-on-write snapshots are a new ownership surface for tenant isolation, and they need a code-level review. This doc-only change is not itself a regression.
